optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Model Evaluation Engineer, Supply Chain Collaboration

professionalSummary.text: Experienced Model Evaluation Engineer with a proven track record of maintaining backtest harnesses, executing pre-release backtests, publishing detailed evaluation reports, and driving forecast accuracy improvements for pilot customers.
professionalSummary.witness: Maintained the backtest harness that replays twelve months of supplier order history per pilot customer and the holdout sets frozen per quarter, both under version control with the forecasting team.

experienceHighlights.text: Maintained a version-controlled backtest harness replaying twelve months of supplier order history per pilot customer and quarterly frozen holdout sets.
experienceHighlights.witness: Maintained the backtest harness that replays twelve months of supplier order history per pilot customer and the holdout sets frozen per quarter, both under version control with the forecasting team.

experienceHighlights.text: Ran pre-release backtests for three model versions and published evaluation reports with per-customer error tables.
experienceHighlights.witness: Ran the pre-release backtest for the three model versions released in the year and published the evaluation report with per-customer error tables.

experienceHighlights.text: Improved weighted forecast error from 24.5% to 17.8% on four pilot customers, meeting documented baseline targets.
experienceHighlights.witness: Weighted forecast error on the four pilot customers fell from 24.5 percent to 17.8 percent between version 1.4 and version 2.0, on the frozen Q3 holdout set and against the documented version 1.4 baseline of 24.5 percent.

experienceHighlights.text: Coordinated release decisions with forecasting lead and customer operations, ensuring clear responsibility boundaries.
experienceHighlights.witness: Coordinated release decisions in the forecasting release meeting; the forecasting lead took the release decision and customer operations confirmed the rollout to each pilot customer.

experienceHighlights.text: Documented backtest assumptions, limitations, and hand-over conditions for each model version.
experienceHighlights.witness: Wrote the backtest notes for each version, listing the holdout composition, the known limitation that promotional periods were excluded from the holdout, and the hand-over items for the next backtest.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Provided a comprehensive evaluation report and backtest notes for version 2.0, including harness run identifiers as a verification trail.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the per-version evaluation report (weighted error per pilot customer, baseline line, version markers) and the backtest notes for version 2.0, with the harness run identifiers as a verification trail.

skills.text: Version control, backtest harness development, forecast accuracy analysis, report writing, stakeholder coordination

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate meets all listed requirements with documented evidence; human review recommended to assess depth of independent improvement work and release decision ownership.

role.roleTitle: Model Evaluation Engineer, Supply Chain Collaboration

evidence.text: Maintained the backtest harness that replays twelve months of supplier order history per pilot customer and the holdout sets frozen per quarter, both under version control with the forecasting team.
Ran the pre-release backtest for the three model versions released in the year and published the evaluation report with per-customer error tables.
evidence.notes: Direct statement of running backtest and publishing report.

evidence.text: Work sample: the per-version evaluation report (weighted error per pilot customer, baseline line, version markers) and the backtest notes for version 2.0, with the harness run identifiers as a verification trail.

Weighted forecast error on the four pilot customers fell from 24.5 percent to 17.8 percent between version 1.4 and version 2.0, on the frozen Q3 holdout set and against the documented version 1.4 baseline of 24.5 percent.
Coordinated release decisions in the forecasting release meeting; the forecasting lead took the release decision and customer operations confirmed the rollout to each pilot customer.

Wrote the backtest notes for each version, listing the holdout composition, the known limitation that promotional periods were excluded from the holdout, and the hand-over items for the next backtest.
